added_claim_errors: "The drug coverage isn't creditable. Then you might need a Part D plan, and possibly Part B to get it" is misleading: Part D eligibility needs Part A or Part B, so Part A alone is enough and Part B is not needed to get a Part D plan.
"10%-per-year lifetime penalty" is imprecise: the penalty is 10% per full 12 months without Part B.

The Federal Register link (govinfo FR-2025-11-19, doc 2025-20251) and the Medicare.gov links are cited as sources. The document number could not be verified from the packet. The $202.90 figure itself matches the key.
"some do; most don't" (plans that require Medicare enrollment at 65) is an unsourced frequency claim.
Names CMS-L564 as the proof form but says only that "your employer fills it out". The asker completes Section A and the employer Section B, so this is incomplete.
The Medicare.gov "Working past 65" and "When can I sign up" URLs and the shiphelp.org link are cited as sources. They could not be verified from the packet, though they are plausible.

Tells the asker to get a "letter stating your coverage start date and that it's based on current employment" as proof for Part B. The required proof is form CMS-L564, which is never named, so this is incomplete and could point the asker to the wrong document.
"Enrolling [in Part A] now is often sensible" is an unsourced judgment, though it is qualified by the HSA caveat.

reasons: Both answers open by telling the asker not to enroll in Part B this month. Both explain that with about 400 employees the group plan pays first and the 8-month Special Enrollment Period avoids the penalty. Both also give the HSA and Part A warning and the Social Security auto-enrollment and decline step. A pulls ahead on three points. It states the 2026 premium ($202.90 a month, about $2,435 a year), so the asker can see what Part B would cost behind the employer plan. It covers creditable drug coverage and the 2-month Part D window. It names CMS-L564, whereas B suggests only an HR letter. B's strengths are asking HR to confirm the coverage is not COBRA or retiree and warning that COBRA does not extend the window. B gives no premium figure, no Part D timing and no CMS-L564, and it also misses the exception for a job or coverage that ends during the Initial Enrollment Period. A has one small error (\"possibly Part B\" to get Part D) and neither mentions the Medigap clock. A's overall coverage of the key is better.
